headline: Oil sinks 8% on Iran diplomacy hopes; dollar slips to one-month low, franc leads
summary: The dollar index fell about 0.4% to near 101.6 after touching a one-month low around 101.45, as an 8% oil slide on US-Iran diplomacy hopes drained haven demand despite a strong ISM. The franc (about +0.75%) and euro (+0.3%) led, while the Aussie (−0.5%), won and Taiwan dollar lagged on pre-RBA selling and Asian equity outflows.
drivers: Oil slump on Iran diplomacy hopes

Brent fell about 8% to near $104 and WTI to about $96 after reports that Trump wants to give talks more time and Iran's leader authorised negotiations. That cut the dollar's haven premium and pulled the index to about 101.45 intraday.
AI-debt worries keep Asia under pressure
The Nasdaq fell about 1% and tech 2.7% on fears of debt-funded AI capex; foreigners sold 374bn won of Korean and about NT$73.5bn of Taiwan shares, pushing USD/KRW to 1,343.8 and USD/TWD to 32.592.
Franc bid, Aussie trimmed before the RBA

The franc rose about 1%, the top G10 gainer, on haven and systematic buying, while the Aussie fell 0.5% below 0.7000 ahead of an expected hike to 4.85%. ISM rose to 55.5 vs 54.5 expected, but prices paid eased to 75.2.
view: Mildly bearish for the next 1–2 weeks: cheaper oil removes the inflation and haven premium, and a December Fed hike is already priced, so good data no longer lifts the dollar much. I fade it against the yen, yuan and ringgit, but not yet against Asian equity-flow currencies like the won and Taiwan dollar. A DXY close back above 102.50 would return me to neutral; a close below 101.40 confirms the downtrend.
ideas: Short 157.50–158.00 as Tokyo guards 160 and the BoJ keeps December live; for 155.00, stop 158.60.
Sold 4.055–4.065 ahead of a possible Bank Negara hike on Nov 5; for 4.010, stop 4.085.
Sold 6.650–6.660 as the PBOC lets the yuan grind to four-year highs; for 6.600, stop 6.675.
review: USD/CAD's short is about 0.4% in favour and USD/CNH's newly filled sale about 0.1%; USD/JPY, AUD/USD and the ringgit sale are 0.2–0.5% against but intact. EUR/USD, EUR/JPY, USD/KRW and USD/TWD were stopped out as the dollar slid against Europe and Asian outflows hit the won and Taiwan dollar, and USD/CHF broke its range; all four move to ranges.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.3% to 1.1189 after a one-month-high push to about 1.1237; Fitch's France warning shrugged off.
eurusd.why: This was a dollar move, not a euro story. An 8% slide in oil on US-Iran diplomacy hopes cut the inflation and haven premium in the dollar, and the index fell about 0.4% to a one-month low. The euro rose despite Fitch moving France's outlook to negative, though it gave back about half the gain into the New York close.
eurusd.outlook: I close the short, stopped at 1.1220, and move to a 1.1130–1.1250 range: cheaper oil helps Europe, but the growth gap and French fiscal worries cap rallies. A close above 1.1250 would open 1.1300.
eurusd.watch: US midterms (Nov 3), euro-area flash CPI, US payrolls (Nov 6), oil and Iran talks.

view.call: 1.1130–1.1250; oil relief vs growth gap, France.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.1% to 1.3404 after topping out near 1.3449, just under the range high.
gbpusd.why: Sterling rode the softer dollar but lagged the euro and franc. UK factory PMI showed the strongest output growth in more than two years, which keeps a Bank of England hike on Thursday near certain, but gilt yields fell about 10bp with oil and trimmed the pound's rate support.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3280–1.3450 range and buy dips: a hawkish BoE hike should hold the floor, but I need a close above 1.3450 to chase it higher.
gbpusd.watch: BoE decision and guidance (Nov 5), UK gilts, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, BoE Nov 5 is the swing.

audusd.note: Down about 0.5% to 0.6996, the weakest major, slipping back under 0.7000 before the RBA.
audusd.why: The Aussie fell on its own side despite a weaker dollar. Traders trimmed longs before Tuesday's RBA decision, where a 25bp hike to 4.85% is widely expected but already about 80% priced, while weak China PMIs, a soft local PMI of 49.6, falling metals-linked sentiment and a 1% Nasdaq drop hurt risk currencies.
audusd.outlook: I keep the long but it is about 0.5% against me: a hike with a hawkish Bullock should lift the pair back toward the 200-day near 0.7066 and on to 0.7130. A close below 0.6970 ends the call.
audusd.watch: RBA decision and Bullock (Nov 3), China trade data, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.25% to 157.95, its first gain in four days, as the yen ignored a softer dollar.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Traders kept unwinding Friday's post-BoJ bounce on doubts about a December hike, and Tokyo's renewed warnings brought little relief. The BoJ's full outlook report said real long-end rates have risen, but with US 10-year yields still near 4.9% the carry gap kept the pair bid even as oil fell.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the short from 157.50–157.80 for 155.00, now about 0.25% against: Tokyo's guard near 159–160 caps the upside and payrolls or a December BoJ signal can drive the turn. A close above 158.60 ends the call.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, BoJ speakers, US midterms (Nov 3) and payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: Short 157.50–158.00; Tokyo caps, BoJ Dec live.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.75% to 0.8187, a break below 0.8200; the franc was the top G10 gainer, up about 1%.
usdchf.why: The franc did the moving. Systematic funds kept buying it as AI-debt worries hit tech stocks and French fiscal risk kept a haven bid, and falling oil eased the dollar's own haven appeal. Swiss sight deposits jumped about 25bn francs last week, a sign the SNB may be leaning against the rise, while positioning already looks stretched.
usdchf.outlook: The old range broke, so I reset to 0.8150–0.8280: crowded franc longs and possible SNB selling should slow the move. A daily close below 0.8150 would open 0.8050.
usdchf.watch: Swiss October CPI (Nov 3), weekly sight deposits (Nov 9), SNB speakers.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.1% to 1.3987, holding near a six-week low as falling oil offset the softer US dollar.
usdcad.why: Two forces cancelled out. WTI fell about 8% to near $96 on signs Washington wants to give Iran diplomacy time, which hit Canada's terms of trade, while the same news drained haven demand from the US dollar. Positive signals on a US-Canada trade deal and last week's BoC hike to 2.50% kept the loonie near its strongest since mid-September.
usdcad.outlook: I keep the short, about 0.4% in favour, for 1.3850: BoC tightening and trade-deal hopes outweigh softer oil. A close above 1.4040 would end the call.
usdcad.watch: Canada jobs (Nov 6), oil and Iran talks, US-Canada trade headlines.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hikes, trade hopes.

usdcnh.note: Down about 0.1% to near 6.6465, the yuan's strongest offshore since June 2022.
usdcnh.why: The yuan rose with the softer dollar and broke 6.65 offshore. The PBOC set the fixing at 6.7146, 521 pips weaker than estimates, to slow the pace of gains, but ANZ noted the fix strengthened by more than 200 pips in October. The PBOC also switched its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repo at 1.25%.
usdcnh.outlook: My sell zone filled; I hold for 6.600 as Beijing allows a slow grind higher. A close above 6.675 would end the call.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China trade data, US midterms (Nov 3).

view.call: Sold 6.650–6.660; PBOC lets the yuan grind up.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.846, still close to the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. A wide gap between US and Hong Kong rates keeps carry traders selling Hong Kong dollars, which holds the pair near the 7.85 weak edge, where the HKMA would buy them to defend the peg.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap pins it near 7.85, and only a sharp rise in HIBOR or HKMA buying would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, Hong Kong Q3 GDP (Nov 3).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.2792 as Asian currencies lagged the dollar's fall against Europe.
usdsgd.why: Regional flows did the moving. The dollar slipped against the euro and franc, but Asian currencies weakened as AI-debt worries kept foreigners selling regional tech stocks and the won and Taiwan dollar fell. The Singapore dollar stayed firm within its trade-weighted band, which the MAS keeps on a strong path.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2720–1.2830 range: a strong S$NEER limits upside, while Asian equity outflows cap gains. A break below 1.2720 needs a broad dollar slide.
usdsgd.watch: US midterms (Nov 3), Singapore PMI, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdkrw.note: Won weakened 9.5 to 1,343.8 at the Seoul close, its first 1,340 handle since Oct 15.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving. Institutions took profit on its recent rally and foreigners sold a net 374bn won of shares even as the Kospi rose 2.2% on dip buying, while Korea's 10-year yield rose about 4bp. Strong October exports were not enough to offset the outflows.
usdkrw.outlook: My short was stopped above 1,343; I move to a 1,330–1,355 range until foreign selling eases. A close above 1,355 would point to 1,370.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, BoK speakers, US midterms (Nov 3) and payrolls (Nov 6).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 11.4 cents to 32.592 at the onshore close after a low of 32.714.
usdtwd.why: Equity outflows did the moving. Foreigners sold about NT$73.5bn of listed shares as AI cash-flow worries pushed the Taiex down 0.65%, after selling about NT$173bn last week, and dividend repatriation added dollar demand. The currency recovered part of its slide in the afternoon as exporters and the central bank leaned against the drop near 32.70.
usdtwd.outlook: My fade was stopped through 32.65; I move to a 32.35–32.75 range, where the central bank caps the weak side. A close above 32.75 would point toward 33.00.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, US tech earnings, Taiwan CPI and exports.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0695/0735 at the 6pm close from 4.0555/0600 after an early 4.0550 high.
usdmyr.why: The ringgit gave back early gains as traders bought dollars ahead of Friday's US payrolls, which are forecast to rise to about 65,000. Hopes that Bank Negara will start normalising rates on Thursday supported it at the open, but softer oil and weaker regional currencies weighed later in the day.
usdmyr.outlook: My sell zone filled and I hold for 4.010: a BNM hike on Nov 5 should restore the ringgit's lead. A close above 4.085 would end the call.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara decision (Nov 5), US payrolls (Nov 6), oil.

usdphp.note: Philippine markets were shut for All Souls' Day; the peso last closed at 63.74 per dollar.
usdphp.why: There was no local trading. The peso's last move was a third straight gain to 63.74 on Friday, still close to its 64.17 record low. The 8% drop in oil helps an importer like the Philippines, while inflation running above 7% and BSP tightening into weak growth still worry investors.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.50–64.20 range: cheaper oil and BSP resolve support the floor, but outflows keep the record low in play. A close above 64.20 could open 65.
usdphp.watch: Philippine October CPI (Nov 5), BSP comments, oil.

usdidr.note: Rupiah eased about 0.1% to 18,140 (Refinitiv) after touching 18,175.
usdidr.why: The rupiah weakened on its own side. Foreign selling of Indonesian assets kept dollar demand firm despite an eight-month-high manufacturing PMI of 54.0, and the governor gave no new signal on intervention. Lower oil and the softer dollar limited the losses.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long for 18,300 on outflows and policy uncertainty; a close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Indonesia October CPI and Q3 GDP (Nov 5), Bank Indonesia operations, foreign bond flows.

usdinr.note: Rupee closed near 94.90, little changed after giving up early gains.
usdinr.why: The rupee barely moved even as Brent fell more than 4% and the dollar slipped. Traders cited strong dollar buying in offshore forwards and expect the RBI to rebuild reserves near 94.50, as its net short forward book swelled to about $240bn in September.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 94.50–95.50 range: the RBI caps both sides and oil sets the drift. A sustained Brent drop below $100 would open 94.20.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, US midterms (Nov 3).

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI caps both ways, oil sets drift.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.5% to near 176.7 as the euro gained and the yen weakened.
eurjpy.why: Both sides worked against the yen. The euro rose about 0.3% with the dollar's broad dip, shrugging off Fitch's negative outlook on France, while the yen slid on doubts that the BoJ will hike in December. That lifted the cross through 177.0 intraday before it eased into the close, with Tokyo's warnings doing little to slow it.
eurjpy.outlook: My short was stopped above 177.0; I step back to a 175.5–177.8 range until the BoJ signals December. A close above 177.8 would open 179.
eurjpy.watch: BoJ speakers, euro-area flash CPI, Tokyo intervention talk.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.3% to near 23.76 as the yuan firmed and the yen slipped.
cnhjpy.why: Both legs pushed it up. The yuan hit its strongest offshore level since June 2022 as the dollar slipped, even though the PBOC set a weaker-than-expected fixing to slow the gains, while the yen fell on doubts about a December BoJ hike. That took the cross to the top of its recent range near 23.8.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.8 range, with no edge until the yen turns or the PBOC slows the yuan.

watch: Next: the RBA, Swiss CPI and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE, Bank Negara and Philippine CPI (Nov 5), US payrolls and Canada jobs (Nov 6), plus oil and Iran talks, AI stocks and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
